parts.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.

result.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 12.7%, Headache 14.0%, Fatigue 15.3%, Dizziness 16.6%, Rash 17.8%, and Transaminase elevation 19.1% [E1]. For the control group in HN-204, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E1]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in HN-204, while Nausea, Headache, Fatigue, Dizziness, and Rash were not serious [E1].

In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 11.8%, Headache 13.0%, Fatigue 14.2%, Dizziness 15.4%, Rash 16.6%, and Transaminase elevation 17.7% [E2]. For the control group in HN-311, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E2]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in HN-311, while Nausea, Headache, Fatigue, Dizziness, and Rash were not serious [E2].

Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the AX-17 % for all listed adverse events was lower in HN-311. Specifically, the AX-17 % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) were: Nausea -0.9 points, Headache -1.0 points, Fatigue -1.1 points, Dizziness -1.2 points, Rash -1.2 points, and Transaminase elevation -1.4 points [E4]. All AX-17 % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points [E4]. The control % for all listed adverse events was the same in both studies, with a difference of +0.0 points for each event when comparing HN-311 to HN-204 [E4].

In both studies, the highest AX-17 % was for Transaminase elevation: 19.1% in HN-204 and 17.7% in HN-311 [E4].
